name: Reporting Under More Than One Standard
title: Reporting Under More Than One Standard
answer: Reporting under more than one standard means preparing financial statements or disclosures that satisfy two or more accounting frameworks at once, such as IFRS and US GAAP, or a local standard plus a parent company standard. The page covers reconciliation, dual reporting, and the systems that track differences in recognition, measurement, and presentation. It also includes how AI tools map line items and notes between frameworks for audit and investor use.

The page covers reconciliation, dual reporting, and the systems that track differences in recognition, measurement, and presentation. It also includes how AI tools map line items and notes between frameworks for audit and investor use.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: This work runs on accounting data warehouses, XBRL tagging systems, and document generation platforms that hold a single chart of accounts with multiple reporting views. The site's company pages and compliance pages provide source material for comparing how firms describe the same transaction under different rules.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by maintaining a mapping table between standards, then applying rule based checks and language models to draft reconciliations and footnote text. Accountants review differences in revenue recognition, leases, financial instruments, and tax. AI can suggest the likely IFRS treatment from a US GAAP entry, but a human approves the final mapping.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Dual reporting creates risk of inconsistent disclosures, audit findings, and regulatory review if one framework is applied incorrectly. The page describes practice rather than advising, so it notes that firms keep version histories of mappings, sign offs from controllers, and clear labels for which standard governs each figure. Data provenance matters because a number may come from a local ledger, a group adjustment, or an AI generated draft.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Reporting under more than one standard is moving toward continuous close and machine readable filings that can be validated against multiple taxonomies at once. As regulators accept structured data, AI tools will likely handle more of the reconciliation and draft disclosure, while accountants focus on judgment areas and exceptions. The site's tracking of compliance and regulation pages will show how new standards converge or diverge over time.
